newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 90 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 90 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 50 billion bolivar ($106 million) auction of 180-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 16.99 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 20 billion bolivars ($42.5 million) in 269-day bills with a 17.34 percent coupon, and another 20 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 17.70 percent coupon.
Fifty billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature Thursday.

Coupons are down from last week's 30 billion bolivar issue when 180-, 269- and 358-day notes carried 18.95, 19.39, and 19.84 percent coupons respectively for effective yields of 16.99, 19.34 and 19.84 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
